To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the national programmes of school leadership development in England and New Zealand are the result of the interaction of a number of factors, including the political, cultural, and ideological contexts of each country, the influence of international agencies and the role played by individuals and organisations in both countries.

The creation of the National College for School Leadership (NCSL) in England and the creation of the National Leadership Academy in New Zealand (NLANZ) have been influenced by the global discourse on leadership and the need for a national approach to leadership development.

In both countries, the introduction of national programmes of school leadership development was a response to the perceived inadequacies in the leadership of schools and the failure to raise standards.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of national programmes for the training and professional development of school leaders.
the creation of national programmes of leadership development in England and New Zealand and the ways in which the two programmes have been implemented in the two countries.
how and why national programmes of school leadership development have been introduced and implemented in England and New Zeal and, in turn, how they have been received by the teaching profession.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both England and New Zealand are moving towards a system where schools are more autonomous, more accountable for results, and more reliant upon the headteacher for their success.
there are many similarities between England and New Zealand in the way that educational reforms have been implemented and the way that schools and teachers are held accountable for student outcomes.

, in both countries, the school principalship has not been considered a profession in its own right and that, in the past, the training and development of school leaders has been a neglected area of policy development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the creation of the National Professional Qualification for Headteachers in England, and the National Principals’ Programme in New Zealand, have both had significant impact on the nature of leadership in schools in both countries.
in both contexts the introduction of school-based management has been the catalyst for the development of national programmes of school leadership development.
in both England and New Zealand there is a need to develop the capacity of school leaders to manage change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many ways to create a national program, and many ways for it to fail.
the development and implementation of school leadership programmes are not straightforward.
there is no one best way to develop school leaders.
